title: Four ears
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday, the first of September. The cover is four ears of corn on the desk, husks on, the lamp. The owner says it's early. Wood says the month's the month. She says the strip has a month now. He says it's had one since '97.

panels.composition: The cover: four ears of corn in their husks on a desk under a lamp's cone.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing four ears of corn in their husks on a desk under a lamp, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner. WOOD. BARNABY.

balloons.text: The strip has a month now.

panels.composition: The owner setting it in the rack. The corn facing the room. September.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner placing a booklet in a wire rack, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Main street from the laundromat door. The school's roof at the end of it, over the trees. Tuesday the buses start. The strip's month.
